pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #5 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A heavy sack of maize has more mass than a small packet of salt. This means the sack has more (1 mark)
   A. Matter
   B. Air only
   C. Light
   D. Sound

2. Which activity shows that air takes up space? (1 mark)
   A. Lighting a candle
   B. Singing a song
   C. Blowing up a balloon
   D. Shining a torch

3. How many grams are in 5 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 50
   B. 500
   C. 5000
   D. 50 000

4. Why should each child use their own balloon for the balloon activity? (1 mark)
   A. To avoid spreading germs
   B. To make it heavier
   C. To make it burst
   D. To make the balloon bigger

5. Which state of matter is used in a cooking gas cylinder? (1 mark)
   A. Powder
   B. Ice
   C. Gas
   D. Solid

6. Which of these is true of a solid? (1 mark)
   A. It takes the shape of any container
   B. It has no mass
   C. It keeps its shape wherever it is put
   D. It cannot be measured

7. Which is the best order of managing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Recycle, reuse, reduce
   B. Reduce, reuse, recycle
   C. Throw, burn, bury
   D. Burn, bury, throw

8. What does reduce mean? (1 mark)
   A. Make less waste
   B. Use again
   C. Burn waste
   D. Make into new items

9. Why should waste bins have lids? (1 mark)
   A. To make waste rot faster
   B. To keep out flies and rats
   C. To make them look nice
   D. To make waste heavier

10. What should you do after handling waste? (1 mark)
   A. Wash hands with soap and clean water
   B. Wipe hands on your clothes
   C. Eat at once
   D. Touch your face

11. Why is broken glass on the ground dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. It feeds the soil
   B. It grows
   C. It can cut people and animals
   D. It rots

12. What is a good use of old clothes? (1 mark)
   A. Burn them near a house
   B. Use them as cleaning cloths
   C. Throw them in a drain
   D. Bury them in a garden pit

13. Which of these is a tool for picking up waste safely? (1 mark)
   A. Bare hands
   B. A towel
   C. A rake
   D. Bare feet

14. What should never be done with waste in a place where children are playing? (1 mark)
   A. Sort it
   B. Burn it
   C. Put it in a bin
   D. Collect it

15. What is a good message for a water conservation poster? (1 mark)
   A. Close the tap after use
   B. Waste is fun
   C. Water is free for all to waste
   D. Leave the tap open

16. A dripping tap fills a 5 litre bucket in one day. How much water is wasted in 4 days? (1 mark)
   A. 1 litre
   B. 54 litres
   C. 20 litres
   D. 9 litres

17. A tap leaks 3 litres each hour. How much is wasted in one day of 24 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 48 litres
   B. 27 litres
   C. 24 litres
   D. 72 litres

18. A tap leaks 2 litres every hour. How much is wasted in 5 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 10 litres
   B. 7 litres
   C. 25 litres
   D. 2 litres

19. Which of these uses less water to wash a car? (1 mark)
   A. A running hose
   B. A large drum poured everywhere
   C. A bucket and sponge
   D. A long shower

20. Why is saving water good for families? (1 mark)
   A. It makes water heavier
   B. It stops rain
   C. It causes floods
   D. It reduces the water bill

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how wasting water can affect other people and the family. (4 marks)

22. Plan a project to sensitise your community about the importance of water conservation. State the steps. (5 marks)

23. Describe how solid waste causes flooding in towns. (4 marks)

24. Suggest two ways to make toys or ornaments from waste and the materials needed. (4 marks)

25. State the difference between mass and volume. (2 marks)

26. Sort into decomposable and non-decomposable: egg shells, tin can, cotton cloth, polythene bag, cow dung, glass bottle. (4 marks)

27. Explain why a kilogram of stones and a kilogram of feathers have the same mass but not the same volume. (4 marks)

28. A jug has 1 litre of juice. 350 ml is poured into a cup. How much is left in the jug? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #5 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Matter
   Mass is the amount of matter.

2. C — Blowing up a balloon
   The balloon swells because air takes up space inside.

3. C — 5000
   5 x 1000 = 5000 g.

4. A — To avoid spreading germs
   Sharing a balloon that has been in someone's mouth can spread germs.

5. C — Gas
   Cooking gas is a gas that burns to give heat.

6. C — It keeps its shape wherever it is put
   A solid has a definite shape.

7. B — Reduce, reuse, recycle
   First make less waste, then reuse, then recycle.

8. A — Make less waste
   To reduce is to make less waste.

9. B — To keep out flies and rats
   Covered bins reduce smell and pests.

10. A — Wash hands with soap and clean water
   Washing removes germs.

11. C — It can cut people and animals
   Sharp glass can injure.

12. B — Use them as cleaning cloths
   Reusing old cloth as cleaning cloths reduces waste.

13. C — A rake
   A rake or shovel keeps hands away from the waste.

14. B — Burn it
   Burning near children is dangerous.

15. A — Close the tap after use
   A short, clear message helps people remember.

16. C — 20 litres
   5 x 4 = 20 litres.

17. D — 72 litres
   3 x 24 = 72 litres.

18. A — 10 litres
   2 x 5 = 10 litres.

19. C — A bucket and sponge
   A bucket limits the water used.

20. D — It reduces the water bill
   Less water used means less money paid.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Less water is left for others, especially in dry areas. The family pays more for water and may have to fetch more.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for others and 2 marks for family.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a message, make posters, put them near taps and gates, speak at assembly, do a demonstration of saving water and check results.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step up to 5.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Polythene bags and plastic block drains. Water cannot flow away when it rains. It gathers in the streets and floods homes and roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 4.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: A toy car from a box and bottle tops. Beads from rolled paper. A flower vase from a tin.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each toy and 1 mark for each list of materials.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and volume is the space it takes up.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct meaning.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decomposable: egg shells, cotton cloth, cow dung. Non-decomposable: tin can, polythene bag, glass bottle.
   Working / marking points: Award 4 marks for all correct, 3 for five, 2 for four and 1 for three.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Both have 1 kg of matter. The feathers take up more space than the stones so their volume is larger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for equal mass, 1 mark for the meaning of mass, 1 mark for feathers taking more space, 1 mark for volume being space.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: 650 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 1 litre = 1000 ml, 1 mark for the subtraction 1000 - 350 and 1 mark for the answer.
